description_full: China Petroleum & Chemical Corporation, an energy and chemical company, engages in the oil and gas and chemical operations in Mainland China. It operates through Exploration and Production, Refining, Marketing and Distribution, Chemicals, and Corporate and Others segments. The company explores and develops oil fields; produces and sells crude oil and natural gas; processes, purifies, imports, and trades in crude oil; manufactures, produces, sells, stores, and trades in petroleum products; owns and operates oil depots and service stations; and produces, markets, distributes, and sells refined petroleum products, including gasoline and diesel. It also manufactures, sells, markets, and distributes petrochemicals and derivative petrochemical products, and other chemical products, such as basic organic chemicals, synthetic resins, synthetic fiber monomers and polymers, synthetic fibers, synthetic rubber, and chemical fertilizers. In addition, the company explores, produces, and sells petroleum and natural gas; produces, stores, transports, and sells petrochemical and coal chemical products; produces and sells catalyst products, lubricant base oil, polyester chips and fibers, plastics, and petrochemical materials; and offers crude oil jetty and natural gas pipeline transmission services. Further, it engages in the production, sale, research, and development of ethylene and downstream byproducts; import and export of petroleum, natural gas, petroleum products, petrochemical, other chemical products, and other commodities and technologies; research, development, and application of technologies and information; hydrogen energy business and related services, such as hydrogen production, storage, transportation, and sales; and battery charging and swapping, solar energy, wind energy, and other new energy business and related services. The company was incorporated in 2000 and is based in Beijing, China. China Petroleum & Chemical Corporation operates as a subsidiary of China Petrochemical Corporation.

financial_summary: China Petroleum & Chemical Corp is a large-cap energy business with a $72.4B market cap on $494.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.
The company is burning through $5.6B of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 4.5×.

Management returns a meaningful 12.6% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 5.7% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.2× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 2% operating margin trails the Energy median (16%) by 13pp, so it is a below-average operator in its field.
It captures well under its share of sector profits (0.21x its revenue share).
It accounts for 12.5% of sector revenue and 2.6% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-22.0% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.05 across 203 companies in the universe; the top four hold 40% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 9% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 17% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 67% and a beta of 0.46, it is more defensive than the market, though its beta has shifted (1y -0.48 vs 5y 0.22), so read it loosely.
Trading is thin (about $2K a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.
In past sell-offs it fell 35% in the 2020 crash and 17% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 72% below its DCF fair value of $2.18, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 31%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $1.74 to $2.77 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.

Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 43% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of -7.7% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 2.0% (vs the 8% bar).
The price implies 12.0% annual cash-flow growth, 19pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 10% earns above the cost of capital of 8.0%, but the 2pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.41).
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.54x.
ROE of 10% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.5x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $1.1B.
The current ratio of 0.78 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 4.8% over 3 years and 7.2% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 24%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
own: Insiders own 5.7%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 34%.
It returns 12.6% a year to shareholders (0.9% in buybacks and 5.0% in dividends).
